# DPP data points

Data points that EU legal acts require, allow or expect in a digital product passport, with their legal basis and what the act says about access. Each data point is defined in one YAML file; this page is generated from those files, so the YAML file is the reference if the two ever differ. The file format is described in [DATAPOINT-FORMAT.md](../DATAPOINT-FORMAT.md).

Data points are reference material for criteria. They are not checked themselves and are not legal advice: which data points apply to a product follows from the delegated or product-specific act for its product group.

Where a published document ties a data point to concepts of open dictionaries, the data point lists their identifiers under "Semantic identifiers": identifiers from the submodel templates of the Industrial Digital Twin Association (IDTA, CC BY 4.0) and IRDIs of the IEC Common Data Dictionary (source: IEC). Only the identifiers are given, no names or definitions of the dictionaries.

## Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (EU) 2024/1781

### Fixed by ESPR for every passport

#### DP-ESPR-001

**Unique product identifier**

EN 18223 attribute: `uniqueProductIdentifier` · access: public · version 1

Persistent unique identifier that the data carrier links to the digital product passport and that gives a web link to it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Term in the legal act | unique product identifier |
| Refers to | model, batch or item, as set by the delegated act |
| Provided by | economic operator, following the identifier scheme |

**Access** The identifier is carried on the product, its packaging or accompanying documents (Art. 10(1)(a), (b)) and a digital copy goes to dealers and online marketplaces (Art. 10(3)(a)). ESPR does not assign it to the public part explicitly, but it is carried on the product and ESPR sets no access restriction for it.

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/oj), Art. 2(30); Art. 10(1)(a), (c); Annex III, point (b) and second paragraph (regulation)

**Semantic identifiers**

From IDTA 02099-1 Digital Product Passport – Part 1 Metadata, version 1.0 (May 2026), submodel template 1.0.2:

- same as IDTA `https://admin-shell.io/idta/cds/uniqueProductIdentifier/1`
- is a case of IDTA `urn:samm:io.admin-shell.idta.dpp.dpp_metadata:1.0.0#uniqueProductIdentifier`
- is a case of IEC CDD `0112/2///61360_7#CBA055#001`
- is a case of IDTA `urn:samm:io.admin-shell.idta.digital_nameplate:3.0.0#uriOfTheProduct`
- is a case of IEC CDD `0112/2///61987#ABN590#002`

Source: [espr/DP-ESPR-001.yaml](espr/DP-ESPR-001.yaml)

#### DP-ESPR-002

**Manufacturer contact details**

access: public · version 1

Name, registered trade name or registered trade mark, postal address with a single contact point and electronic means of communication of the manufacturer, in the public part of the digital product passport.

| | |
|---|---|
| Term in the legal act | manufacturer name, registered trade name or registered trade mark, postal address, electronic means of communication |
| Refers to | model, or as set by the delegated act |
| Provided by | manufacturer |

**Access** Art. 27(6), first subparagraph, point (a) places the details on the public part of the passport, where applicable. Missing or incorrect details are a formal non-compliance under Art. 71(1)(g).

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/oj), Art. 27(6), first subparagraph, point (a), and second subparagraph; Annex III, point (g); Art. 71(1)(g) (regulation)

Source: [espr/DP-ESPR-002.yaml](espr/DP-ESPR-002.yaml)

#### DP-ESPR-003

**Digital instructions for use**

access: public · version 1

Instructions for use in digital format, included in the digital product passport and accessible via the data carrier. They contain at least the information under Art. 7(2)(b)(ii), as provided for in the delegated act.

| | |
|---|---|
| Term in the legal act | digital instructions for use |
| Refers to | model, or as set by the delegated act |
| Provided by | manufacturer |

**Access** Art. 27(7), third subparagraph, requires the instructions to be included in the passport and made accessible via the data carrier. The fourth subparagraph keeps them online and downloadable for at least ten years, and the fifth requires a free paper copy on request. No access restriction is set, but ESPR does not use the term public part here.

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 (ESPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1781/oj), Art. 27(7), first, third and fourth subparagraphs; Art. 29(4); Art. 30(2)(b); Art. 7(8) (regulation)

Source: [espr/DP-ESPR-003.yaml](espr/DP-ESPR-003.yaml)

## Toy Safety Regulation (EU) 2025/2509

### Required by the product-specific regulation

#### DP-TOY-001

**Toy DPP data catalogue**

access: set by the delegated act · version 1

Self-contained list of fields: mandatory information under Art. 19(2)(b) and (c) in conjunction with Annex VI, Part I, points (a) to (n), and optional information under Annex VI, Part II.

| | |
|---|---|
| Term in the legal act | toy digital product passport (Regulation (EU) 2025/2509) |
| Refers to | model (Art. 19(2)(a)); batch where other Union law requires the batch level (Art. 19(9)) |
| Provided by | manufacturer (Art. 19(1)) |

**Access** Summary row of the toy data catalogue. Art. 19(2)(f) opens the passport to consumers and other end users, market surveillance and customs authorities, notified bodies, the Commission and other economic operators, free of charge (Art. 20(3)), according to the access rights set by the delegated act under Art. 49(1)(d). The regulation does not assign access per data point. That delegated act must balance trade secrets under Directive (EU) 2016/943 against easy consumer access (Art. 49(1), second subparagraph).

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2025/2509 (toy safety)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2025/2509/oj), Art. 19; Art. 20; Art. 21; Art. 22; Art. 49; Art. 59; Annex VI (regulation)

Source: [toy/DP-TOY-001.yaml](toy/DP-TOY-001.yaml)

#### DP-TOY-002

**Statement of demonstrated conformity**

## Construction Products Regulation (EU) 2024/3110

### Required by the product-specific regulation

#### DP-CPR-001

**Construction product passport data catalogue**

access: set by the delegated act · version 1

Mandatory content of the construction product passport under Art. 76(2)(a)(i) to (vii): the declaration of performance and conformity, product information under Annex IV, technical documentation, markings, identifiers, documents required by other Union law, and data carriers of essential components. This entry summarises the construction product data catalogue.

| | |
|---|---|
| Term in the legal act | construction product digital product passport (Regulation (EU) 2024/3110) |
| Refers to | product type (Art. 76(2)(d); Art. 77(1)(a), (f)) |
| Provided by | manufacturer; other actors enter or update data as set by the delegated act (Art. 75(2)(d)) |

**Access** Summary row for the construction product data catalogue. The passport is accessible free of charge through the data carrier to all economic operators, customers, users and authorities (Art. 76(2)(e)), and the system supports different access levels (Art. 76(2)(f)). The delegated act under Art. 75(1) sets the access level per information item and protects trade secrets and intellectual property rights (Art. 75(2)(c); Art. 77(1)(g); Art. 78(b), (f), (g)).

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2024/3110 (CPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/3110/oj), Art. 15; Art. 16; Art. 22; Art. 75 to 79; Annex II; Annex IV; Annex V (regulation)

Source: [cpr/DP-CPR-001.yaml](cpr/DP-CPR-001.yaml)

#### DP-CPR-002

**Declaration of performance and conformity**

access: public · version 1

Declaration following the model in Annex V. It states the performance in relation to the essential characteristics and, where product requirements under Art. 7 apply, compliance with them. Its parts are DP-CPR-003 to DP-CPR-045.

| | |
|---|---|
| Term in the legal act | declaration of performance and conformity |
| Refers to | product type |
| Provided by | manufacturer |

**Access** Openly available as part of the declaration of performance and conformity: an electronic copy accompanies each product made available unless the passport contains it (Art. 16(1)), and it may be provided on a continuously available website with free access for recipients (Art. 16(2)(c), (d)). The passport is reachable through the data carrier (Art. 76(2)(e)). Finer access levels are left to the delegated act under Art. 75(1).

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2024/3110 (CPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/3110/oj), Art. 76(2)(a)(i); Art. 15; Art. 16(1); Art. 77(1)(h); Annex V (regulation)

#### DP-CPR-069

**Technical documentation**

access: set by the delegated act · version 1

Declared intended use, evidence for performance and conformity, the procedures under Art. 22(4), details of the assessment and verification system and, where relevant, simplified procedures (Art. 59 to 61).

| | |
|---|---|
| Term in the legal act | technical documentation |
| Refers to | product type |
| Provided by | manufacturer |

**Access** The technical documentation under Art. 22(3) is passport content (Art. 76(2)(a)(iii)). CPR assigns it no access level; it is a typical case for the protection of trade secrets and intellectual property rights under Art. 78(g). The passport is accessible free of charge via the data carrier to all economic operators, customers, users and authorities (Art. 76(2)(e)), and the system allows different access levels (point (f)). The delegated act under Art. 75(1) sets the level for each piece of information (Art. 75(2)(c); Art. 77(1)(g); Art. 78(b), (f)) and protects trade secrets and intellectual property rights (Art. 78(g)).

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2024/3110 (CPR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/3110/oj), Art. 76(2)(a)(iii); Art. 22(3)(a) to (e); Art. 59 to 61 (regulation)

The passport is accessible free of charge via the data carrier to all economic operators, customers, users and authorities (Art. 76(2)(e)), and the system allows different access levels (point (f)). The delegated act under Art. 75(1) sets the level for each piece of information (Art. 75(2)(c); Art. 77(1)(g); Art. 78(b), (f)) and protects trade secrets and intellectual property rights (Art. 78(g)).

**Basis**

## Deforestation Regulation (EU) 2023/1115

### Required by sectoral law outside the DPP rules

#### DP-EUDR-001

**Due diligence statement reference number or simplified declaration identification number**

access: not specified · version 1

Operators submit the due diligence statement and receive a reference number; micro or small primary operators submit a one-off simplified declaration and receive an identification number. Downstream operators and traders do not submit a due diligence statement; only the first downstream actor records and keeps the numbers.

| | |
|---|---|
| Term in the legal act | reference number of the due diligence statement / identification number of the simplified declaration |
| Refers to | consignment or product |
| Provided by | information system (Art. 33); recorded by the operator or the first downstream actor |

**Access** Mandatory outside DPP law, under Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650. ESPR sets no access rule for it. EUDR due diligence data are in principle meant for authorities and the supply chain, not for the public.

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 (EUDR), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1115/oj), Art. 4; Art. 4a; Art. 5; Art. 33 (regulation)

Source: [eudr/DP-EUDR-001.yaml](eudr/DP-EUDR-001.yaml)

#### DP-EUDR-002

**Due diligence information**

access: not specified · version 1

Information that the operator must collect and keep, including a description with the species of wood, quantity, country of production, geolocation, time of production, suppliers, and evidence that the products are deforestation-free and legal. Micro or small primary operators may give the address of the plots of land or of the establishment instead of the geolocation.

| | |
|---|---|
| Term in the legal act | information referred to in Article 9(1) |
| Refers to | consignment |
| Provided by | operator; suppliers |

**Access** Mandatory outside DPP law, under Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650. ESPR sets no access rule for it. EUDR due diligence data are in principle meant for authorities and the supply chain, not for the public.

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2023/1115 (EUDR), as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2650](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1115/oj), Art. 9(1) (regulation)

Source: [eudr/DP-EUDR-002.yaml](eudr/DP-EUDR-002.yaml)

## Batteries Regulation (EU) 2023/1542

Battery passports are required from 18 February 2027 for LMT batteries, industrial batteries with a capacity greater than 2 kWh and electric vehicle batteries (Art. 77(1)). The data points follow the numbering, the battery categories and the applicability of the European Commission's [Guidance Document: Digital Batteries Passport – data points by category, version 2.0 of 15 August 2026](https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/document/download/cd1e5e6c-4a4a-4b99-995a-49eb6916187e_en) (© European Union, 2026, CC BY 4.0); names and descriptions are paraphrased and the access and granularity entries are added from the Regulation. The guidance is not legally binding.

### Required by the product-specific regulation

#### DP-BATT-001

**Unique battery identifier**

EN 18223 attribute: `uniqueProductIdentifier` · access: public · version 1

Unique identifier that the economic operator placing the battery on the market attributes to the battery; the QR code on the battery links to it and gives access to the battery passport.

| | |
|---|---|
| Term in the legal act | unique identifier |
| Refers to | individual battery |
| Provided by | economic operator that places the battery on the market (Art. 77(4)); after preparation for re-use, repurposing or remanufacturing, or when the battery becomes waste, the operator named in Art. 77(7) |

**Access** Art. 77(3) makes the battery passport accessible through the QR code that links to this identifier; the Regulation sets no access restriction for it.

| Battery category | Applicability |
|---|---|
| Electric vehicle batteries | mandatory |
| LMT batteries | mandatory |
| Industrial batteries > 2 kWh | mandatory |

**Basis**

- [Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 (Batteries)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1542/oj), Art. 77(3), first subparagraph (regulation)
- [European Commission, Guidance Document: Digital Batteries Passport – data points by category, version 2.0 of 15 August 2026](https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/document/download/cd1e5e6c-4a4a-4b99-995a-49eb6916187e_en), data point 1 (guidance)

**Semantic identifiers**

From IDTA 02099-1 Digital Product Passport – Part 1 Metadata, version 1.0 (May 2026), submodel template 1.0.2:

- same as IDTA `https://admin-shell.io/idta/cds/uniqueProductIdentifier/1`
- is a case of IDTA `urn:samm:io.admin-shell.idta.dpp.dpp_metadata:1.0.0#uniqueProductIdentifier`
- is a case of IEC CDD `0112/2///61360_7#CBA055#001`
- is a case of IDTA `urn:samm:io.admin-shell.idta.digital_nameplate:3.0.0#uriOfTheProduct`
- is a case of IEC CDD `0112/2///61987#ABN590#002`

Source: [batt/DP-BATT-001.yaml](batt/DP-BATT-001.yaml)

**Access** The Regulation sets no access restriction for the identity of the responsible operator.

| Battery category | Applicability |

**Basis**

- [European Commission, Guidance Document: Digital Batteries Passport – data points by category, version 2.0 of 15 August 2026](https://single-market-economy.ec.europa.eu/document/download/cd1e5e6c-4a4a-4b99-995a-49eb6916187e_en), data point 2 (guidance)
